gauges.name: Wisconsin River at Rothschild
gauges.description: Primary gauge for the Wausau metro area

tips.Walleye: Jigs tipped with minnows near current breaks and dam tailwaters. Best at dawn/dusk. Try 1/4 oz jig heads bounced along sandy bottoms.
tips.Smallmouth Bass: Crankbaits and tube jigs around rocky shorelines and bridge pilings. Topwater action in summer evenings.
tips.Musky: Large bucktails and jerkbaits along weed edges and deep structure. Fall is prime — focus on figure-8s at the boat.
tips.Channel Catfish: Cut bait or stink bait on the bottom near deeper holes. Night fishing in summer is most productive.
tips.Sturgeon: Catch-and-release only. Observe from shore during the spring spawning run — a spectacular sight near Rothschild dam.

season_notes: Walleye/Sauger open first Sat in May
Catch-and-release bass season Mar–Jun

tips.Smallmouth Bass: Crawfish-pattern crankbaits and ned rigs along the rocky banks below the dam.
tips.Musky: Trolling large crankbaits through the deeper pools downstream. Look for baitfish schools on electronics.
tips.Channel Catfish: Chicken liver or nightcrawlers fished on bottom rigs in the slower pools below the dam.

gauges.name: Big Rib River at Rib Falls

tips.Brook Trout: Small spinners (#0–#2 Mepps) and worms in the upper Class I reaches. Wade quietly upstream — brookies spook easily.
tips.Brown Trout: Larger streamers and Rapala minnows in the deeper pools. Best fishing is early morning or after dark in summer.
tips.Smallmouth Bass: Small crankbaits and soft plastics in the lower reaches near Rib Falls. Look for them near log jams.

gauges.name: Eau Claire River near Kelly
gauges.description: Major eastern tributary of the Wisconsin River

tips.Smallmouth Bass: Tube jigs and soft plastic crawfish along rocky runs. The Eau Claire has excellent wade fishing for bronzebacks.
tips.Walleye: Jig and minnow combos in deeper pools near Kelly dam. Evening and night fishing most productive.
tips.Brown Trout: Found in the cooler upper reaches. Drift nymphs or swing wet flies through the riffles.

gauges.name: Big Eau Pleine River at Stratford
gauges.description: Feeds the Eau Pleine Reservoir southwest of Wausau

tips.Walleye: Jig and minnow near the reservoir inlet in spring. Troll crankbaits along drop-offs in summer.
tips.Northern Pike: Spinnerbaits and large spoons along weed edges. Spring pike stack up near creek inlets after ice-out.
tips.Panfish: Small jigs tipped with wax worms near submerged timber. Excellent ice fishing for crappie and bluegill in winter.
tips.Largemouth Bass: Texas-rigged soft plastics and spinnerbaits around fallen trees and lily pad edges in summer.

season_notes: Walleye open first Sat in May
Reservoir influence — good ice fishing in winter

gauges.name: Prairie River near Merrill
gauges.description: Designated trout stream north of Wausau near Merrill

tips.Brook Trout: Small spinners (#0–#2 Mepps) or live worms in the upper reaches. Wade upstream quietly — brookies hold in cold, shaded pools and undercut banks.
tips.Brown Trout: Streamers and Rapala minnows through the deeper runs. Best early morning or after dark. Dry fly action in summer evenings with caddis and PMD patterns.
tips.Rainbow Trout: Drift nymphs (hare's ear, pheasant tail) through the riffles. Egg patterns effective in fall. Check DNR stocking reports for timing.

season_notes: Early catch-and-release season opens first Sat in Jan

gauges.name: Wisconsin River at Wisconsin Rapids
gauges.description: Main stem downstream of Wausau — largest city in the chain

tips.Walleye: Jig and minnow combos in the deep holes near the Wisconsin Rapids dam. Spring walleye run draws anglers from across the state.
tips.Smallmouth Bass: Tubes and crawfish-pattern crankbaits along the rocky banks — strong smallmouth population.
tips.Musky: Trolling large crankbaits through the deeper pools and along current breaks downstream of the dam.
tips.Channel Catfish: Cut bait or chicken liver in the deeper pools below the dam at night.
tips.White Bass: Small spoons and inline spinners during the spring run — schools of fish stack up below the dam.

season_notes: Walleye/Sauger open first Sat in May

gauges.description: Iconic Class I trout & whitewater destination northeast of Wausau

tips.Brook Trout: Small spinners and dry flies in the upper reaches and feeder streams. The Wolf has a strong native population.
tips.Smallmouth Bass: Tube jigs and topwater poppers in the slower stretches and pools downstream of the rapids.
tips.Walleye: Found in the deeper runs and below the rapids — jig and minnow combos work well.

gauges.name: Tomorrow River near Nelsonville
gauges.description: Class I trout stream destination near Stevens Point

tips.Brown Trout: One of central Wisconsin's premier brown trout streams. Drift hopper-dropper rigs through the riffles, or fish streamers in the deeper runs at dawn and dusk.
tips.Brook Trout: Small Mepps spinners or dry flies in the upper reaches. Native population — handle with care if releasing.

regulations.rule: Some sections have artificial-lure-only and special length regs — check DNR maps

upcoming_events.name: Inland Trout Season Closes
upcoming_events.description: Last day for inland trout on streams, springs, and spring ponds. The Prairie, Little Plover, Tomorrow, and Rib tributaries all close until the early catch-and-release period in January.

upcoming_events.name: Early Catch-and-Release Trout Opens
upcoming_events.description: Winter catch-and-release trout season opens on inland streams (artificials only). Runs until the regular season opener in April.

upcoming_events.name: Free Fishing Weekend (Winter)
upcoming_events.description: Jan. 16–17. No license or stamps required for residents or nonresidents — a great weekend to try ice fishing. All bag/size limits still apply.

upcoming_events.name: General Inland Game Fish Season Closes
upcoming_events.description: Walleye, northern pike, and most inland game fish seasons close on inland waters until the first Saturday in May.
